messages:
Maria G.: Quick heads-up — ran a 1k-sample mini-bakeoff for faultline-7b across fp16 / int8 / int6. Mixed GPU/CPU infra; sharing raw numbers + a couple odd regressions.
Ryan K.: awesome — drop perf + rough unit-costs?
Maria G.: paste from the run:```
model | p95_ms | rps | est $ / 1k tokens
faultline-7b fp16 | 150 | 120 | 0.12
faultline-7b int8  | 160 | 110 | 0.08
faultline-7b int6  | 170 | 105 | 0.06
```
Sophie L.: quality deltas? numbers or quick examples.
Maria G.: eval on 200-sample open_qa subset: fp16 EM=0.72, int8 EM=0.70, int6 EM=0.62. int6 drop concentrated on multi-hop and long-context prompts (>=200 tokens).
David P.: any hallucination / safety regressions flagged?
Maria G.: two clear hallucination cases with int6 where the model invented a citation. Example (short):
> prompt: "Summarize the main findings of the paper on adaptive caching."
> fp16 answer: correct summary + cites 'Zhang et al. 2022' (real)
> int6 answer: plausible-looking summary that fabricates a paper title and link.
Ryan K.: rough math on the unit-costs? how did you get $/1k token figures?
Maria G.: We used: est_cost = (GPU_hourly / tokens_per_hour) * 1000. Assumptions: GPU price $2.4/hr for the infra we used, measured tokens/s during steady-state: fp16=33k tokens/s, int8=50k tokens/s, int6=66k tokens/s (these vary by batch). I included network+overhead fudge ~10%.
Sophie L.: So int6 saves ~50% vs fp16 but drops ~14 pt EM on multi-hop — feels risky for product.
David P.: Could we route by prompt features? short/simple -> int6, long/complex -> fp16. We already have an L0 classifier for difficulty.
Maria G.: Exactly my thinking. Quick sim using our 10k production sample and a cheap difficulty classifier: routing 70% to int6 and 30% to fp16 gives blended cost ~0.07 $/1k and blended EM ~0.69 (vs baseline 0.72) — acceptable for some non-critical endpoints.
Ryan K.: Any latency tail issues when falling back from int6->fp16?
Maria G.: FP16 fallback adds ~200ms extra for the client if synchronous; for async/backfill it's fine. Tail p99: int6 has slightly higher p99 compared to fp16 because of CPU fallback in some nodes.
Sophie L.: For GTN/product: recommend default routing to int8, not int6, unless cost pressure is extreme. Int8 gives small quality loss (0.02 EM) but decent savings.
David P.: Agreed. Proposal: default int8 with these flags: route_on <=120 tokens -> int8; >120 -> fp16; and enable predictive difficulty classifier for 5% of traffic as canary to validate.
Maria G.: Action items: 1) Run a 10k slice sim (I will) with our product prompts; 2) Expand regression tests for hallucination signatures on int6; 3) Create a small rollout plan (canary 1% -> 10% -> 50%).
Ryan K.: please add the rollout plan to the canary doc when you have results.
Sophie L.: +1 on regression tests. Also add a tiny human-review set for multi-hop examples.
david p.: @Maria G. want help with the sim? I can wire up the classifier and run the slice tomorrow.
Maria G.: thanks — will ping when I push the dataset to the bench infra.
eval-bot: smoke test: mini-bench artifacts uploaded to /bench/runs/1799998888 (checksums OK) :white_check_mark:
Sophie L.: :thumbsup:
Ryan K.: good start — this gives product actionable guidance. Keep us posted on the 10k sim.
Maria G.: will do — tagging this thread for follow-up after the larger sim completes.
